sentences.text: Shri Akhilesh Kumar Saxena, learned counsel for the peti  Ms. Vinita Dwivedi, learned Panel Lawyer for the respond Shri Pankaj Joshi, learned counsel for the respondent.
Heard on I.A. No.1532/2024, which is first application filed under Section 389 of the Criminal Procedure Code, 1973 for suspension of sentence on behalf of appellant.

2. The appellant has been convicted for sentence under Sections 376 & 450 of IPC, 1860 and sentenced to undergo 10 years R.I. and 5 years R.I. with fine of Rs.1,000/- & Rs.500/- and default stipulations.
3 . Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant is innocent and has falsely been implicated.
The appellant has already suffered approximately two years in his incarceration.
The prosecutrix has married with the appellant.
Due to misconception, the FIR was lodged.
Now, they have settled their matter and they want to live together.
He further submits that the prosecutrix has no objection for grant of bail to the appellant.
In support, the prosecutrix has also filed an affidavit.
There are material contradictions and omissions in the statement of the prosecution witnesses.
He further submitted that final hearing of this appeal is likely to take sufficient long time.
Under these circumstances, learned counsel prays that the application for suspension of sentence of the appellant be allowed.
4. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of prosecutrix/objector has also submitted the prosecutrix has no objection regarding suspension of sentence of the appellant.
5. Learned counsel for the State opposed the prayer and prayed for dismissal of the application for suspension of sentence.

6. Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, contention of learned counsel for the appellant and custody period of the appellant, without commenting on the merits of the case, the application Morsingh @ Mohrasingh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19975768/
1 is allowed.

sentences.text: 7. It is directed that subject to depositing the fine amount, if already not deposited, the appellant shall be released on bail, on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) with a solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of Trial Court, for his appearance before the Registry of this Court firstly on 12.08.2024 and on such other dates, as may be fixed by the Registry in this regard, till final disposal of this appeal.
8. Accordingly, I.A. No. 1532/2024 stands allowed and disposed of.

(PREM NARAYAN SINGH) JUDGE Vindesh Morsingh @ Mohrasingh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19975768/
